request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A change that alters any person's overdue-total is now also followed by the rollup lines, and
every ROLLUP line gains overdue-total=<overdue-total> at its end, every TOTALS line
overdue-total=<total> at its end (a TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moved).
A change of the sheet's today that puts a claim past its due-by, or takes one out of overdue, is
such a change even when no due or due-total moved.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Done. `bin/e2e` builds and runs, and all 4 acceptance tests pass.

The whole change is in the server, in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/RollupService.java`:

- **New figure tracked:** before and after each change, the service now also works out each person's overdue-total and the sheet's overall overdue-total. This copies how the screen does it: add up the dues of a person's counted claims that are OPEN or PENDING with a due-by before the sheet's today. Claims with no due (n/a) are skipped, and the total is not held down to the cap.
- **When lines are written:** a ROLLUP line is now also written when only a person's overdue-total moved. A TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moved.
- **Line format:** `overdue-total=<value>` is added at the end of every ROLLUP and TOTALS line. The existing fields keep their order.
- **Changing the sheet's today:** this already compared figures before and after, so it now writes the lines whenever a claim goes into or out of overdue, even if no due or due-total changed.

One small choice: a claim with no due-by is never counted as overdue. That is also how the screen behaves.
